AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 7, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-15-21, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE
FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING
THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709
573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a)
  – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County Sheriff representative, and other related City
  officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Numbers 8056-015-014, 8056-015-016, and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Michael F G Trust; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Mr. Deepak Hira
  The Sindhu Center

FLAG SALUTE
  Rianah Bonifacio
  Santa Fe High School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS None scheduled.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Athens Disposal - Senate Bill 1383 video.

  3.  Sprouts Market Groundbreaking video.

  4.  Thanksgiving Food Distribution video.

  5.  Tree Lighting and Festival video.

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  November 4 and 16, 2021. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the periods October 17, 2021 –
  October 30, 2021, in the total amount of $994,535.55 and October 31, 2021 – November 13, 2021, in
  the total amount of $953,492.23. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  November 11, 2021 – November 24, 2021, in the total amount of $3,191,054.12. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Margarita
  Acosta and Jesus Salvador. 830-01/19

  Report

  5.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-73 – BUDGET AMENDMENT AND AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR
  PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR UNITED STATES BUREAU OF RECLAMATION
  WATERSMART GRANT APPLICATION SUPPORT – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-73, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE MEASURE W SAFE CLEAN WATER FUNDS FOR
  PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR UNITED STATES BUREAU OF
  RECLAMATION WATERSMART GRANT APPLICATION SUPPORT, in the amount of $22,816;
  and

  b.  award a contract to Arcadis U.S. Inc., in the amount of $19,840 to provide professional engineering
  services for United States Bureau of Reclamation WaterSmart grant application support; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 310-02/610

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 4 - CRISIS COMMUNICATION SERVICES AGREEMENT - Staff
  recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 4 to the crisis communication consulting services
  agreement with Merino, Barajas & Associates, Inc. not to exceed $114,000; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute this amendment, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  710-07

  Report

  8.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-74 - AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 TO
  INCORPORATE THE 2022 CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE REQUIREMENTS – Staff recommends
  City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-74, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
   NORWALK AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 FOR GENERAL AND
  HOURLY UNIT EMPLOYEES AND EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT UNIT
  EMPLOYEES TO INCORPORATE THE 2022 CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE REQUIREMENTS. 135-
  03

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  9.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  10. AGREEMENT FOR PUBLIC AFFAIRS AND COMMUNICATION SERVICES - Staff recommends City
  Council approve an agreement with Merino, Barajas & Associates, Inc. not to exceed $72,000 from
  October 31, 2021 through June 30, 2022; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement on
  behalf of the City, and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney. 135-07

  Report

  11. APPROVAL OF EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATION AGREEMENT FOR THE POTENTIAL DEVELOPMENT
  OF A PROJECT WITHIN THE HEART OF NORWALK PROJECT AREA INCLUDING CITY-OWNED
  PARCELS (ASSESSOR PARCEL NUMBERS 8056-015-014/016/020) – Staff recommends City
  Council approve an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement with Primestor Development, Inc. to establish the
  terms and conditions of a Disposition and Development Agreement for City-owned parcels and the
  subject properties located at 13400 San Antonio Drive, also known as (APNs 8056-015-014, 8056-015-
  016, and 8056-015-020); and authorize the City Manager to execute the Term Sheet and agreement
  and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney. 1405-06

  Report

  12. CLOSURE OF CITY OPERATIONS FROM DECEMBER 27 TO DECEMBER 30, 2021 – Staff
  recommends City Council approve:

  a.  the allocation of 36 hours of Mental Health Break to full-time employees and 12 hours of Mental
  Health Break to part-time employees; and

  b.  the closure of City Hall and other City facilities from December 27 to December 30, 2021, with the
  exception of some essential City services in the Public Safety, Public Services, Transportation,
  Recreation, and Social Services Departments. 135-01-04

  Report

  13. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – DECEMBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated December 3, 2021.
 Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
